universal_lens: Off-the-ball positional influence as a geometric proxy for defensive gravity, modeled via dynamic opponent proximity relative to a compactness baseline. Spatial defensive proximity metrics quantify geometrically instantaneous baseline deviations, not causal attraction or psychological attention.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference of player impact using optical tracking data, conditioning on spatial configurations and opponent behavior to estimate construct validity. Bayesian inference maps defensive proximity to probabilistic player engagement models using minute-equivalent gravity as evidence for tactical positioning.
gse_mapping: Situationally grounded state transitions in football dynamics, where player positions trigger opponent repositioning, encoded via frame-by-frame geometric proximity metrics. Situational reasoning transitions between frames by accumulating pull(p,t)×Δt to compute evolving gravity states, enabling dynamic threat assessment.

primitives.name: Magnet Player
primitives.verbatim_quote: SPORTS ANALYTICS · OPTICAL TRACKING · FOOTBALL The Magnet Player: a geometric proxy for off-theball offensive gravity in football, from optical tracking data A player can change a match without touching the ball, if their position alone forces the opponent to move.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'player index (dimensionless)', 'O_i': 'opponent i position vector (meters)', 'M_P': 'magnet player position vector (meters)', 'd_{PO}': 'distance between player P and opponent O (meters)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are modeled as points in 2D space; opponent movement is reactive to player position; proximity is inversely related to defensive attention.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When d_{PO} approaches zero, opponent proximity becomes singular and dominant.

layer2.mapping: Maps positional influence to defensive displacement using inverse-distance weighting from opponent positions relative to a compactness baseline.
layer2.telemetry: Frame-by-frame opponent displacement vectors and associated spatial entropy.

primitives.name: Defensive Gravity
primitives.verbatim_quote: The idea is inspired by the shooting "gravity" popularized in NBA basketball with Second Spectrum's optical tracking in the mid2010s, with a direct academic antecedent in the statistical characterization of defensive skill via spatial tracking by Franks et al.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G_P': 'defensive gravity generated by player P (dimensionless)', 'r_{ij}': 'relative distance between player P and opponent j (meters)', 'R_{baseline}': 'compactness baseline radius (meters)', 'k': 'scaling factor for gravity strength (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Gravity is proportional to inverse square of distance; baseline reflects normal compactness of opponent group.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When r_{ij} < R_{baseline}, gravity increases rapidly; when r_{ij} >> R_{baseline}, gravity approaches zero.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to NBA shooting gravity model adapted for football’s spatial dynamics and opponent reaction patterns.
layer2.telemetry: Opponent movement deviation from baseline trajectory over time windows.

primitives.name: Positional Value Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: ABSTRACT Football analytics is good at measuring on-ball value (expected goals, expected threat, packing) and poor at measuring value off it.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'PV_i': 'positional value index for player i (dimensionless)', 'C_i': 'compactness measure around player i (meters^2)', 'N_{opp}': 'number of opponents within radius (dimensionless)', 'T_{frame}': 'time interval per frame (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player influence scales with opponent density and spatial exclusion; time-normalized for consistency across frames.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N_{opp} = 0, PV_i = 0; when N_{opp} → ∞, PV_i saturates due to compactness limits.

layer2.mapping: Quantifies off-ball value through opponent spatial exclusion and temporal clustering around player position.
layer2.telemetry: Spatial entropy and opponent clustering coefficient per player per frame.

primitives.name: Construct Validity Check
primitives.verbatim_quote: It proposes a formal three-level validation program, covering construct, convergent and predictive validity, with explicit hypotheses to close that distance.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'CV_{construct}': 'construct validity score (dimensionless)', 'CV_{convergent}': 'convergent validity score (dimensionless)', 'CV_{predictive}': 'predictive validity score (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Validity scores are normalized between 0 and 1; each level independently assesses model fidelity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: All CV scores must exceed threshold α = 0.7 for acceptable validity.

layer2.mapping: Maps the proposed validation framework onto standard psychometric models of construct validity in sports analytics.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation matrices between derived metrics and known behavioral outcomes.

primitives.name: Spatial Defensive Proximity
primitives.verbatim_quote: This metric quantifies spatial defensive proximity relative to the match's instantaneous baseline, not causal defensive attraction.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'pull(p,t)': 'dimensionless ratio of actual to baseline distance', 'Δt': '0.5 seconds per frame'}
primitives.assumptions: Baseline is computed as maximum of 3.5 meters and average player distance per frame.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When multiple opponents approach simultaneously, pull(p,t) exceeds 1.

layer2.mapping: Gravity(p) = Σt pull(p, t) × Δt serves as kernel for GSE state transition functions.
layer2.telemetry: Minute-equivalents of defensive proximity per player per match.

primitives.name: Geometric Offensive Gravity
primitives.verbatim_quote: Put differently: what follows is the construction of a geometric proxy for offensive gravity, not of demonstrated offensive gravity.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'gravity_minutes': 'unit representing accumulated geometric influence over time'}
primitives.assumptions: Offensive gravity is modeled via spatial relationships rather than behavioral intent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Not applicable; defined as a proxy for geometric influence only.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's offensive engagement tensor, mapping geometric pull to tactical risk.
layer2.telemetry: Accumulated gravity minutes per player per match.

primitives.name: Minute-Equivalent Accumulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The correction multiplies each frame by the real time it represents (0.5 seconds, at production sampling) and accumulates the result in minutes: MATCH TOTAL, IN MINUTE-EQUIVALENTS Gravity(p) = Σt pull(p, t) × Δt On the unit's name, an explicit correction relative to an earlier version of this manuscript.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Gravity(p)': 'minute-equivalents of defensive proximity', 'pull(p,t)': 'ratio of current to baseline distance', 'Δt': '0.5 seconds per frame'}
primitives.assumptions: Each frame contributes proportional time weight to total gravity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pull(p,t) > 1, total may represent multiple simultaneous influences.

layer2.mapping: Used as core temporal accumulation kernel in GSE state evolution logic.
layer2.telemetry: Total gravity minutes per player across match duration.

primitives.name: Baseline Compactness
primitives.verbatim_quote: Anyone who wishes can reproduce every number with a calculator.
primitives.assumptions: Baseline adjusts dynamically based on average player spacing, capped at 3.5m.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Goalkeepers with large own_dist contribute disproportionately to baseline.

layer2.mapping: Provides normalized reference for pull(p,t) calculations in GSE.
layer2.telemetry: Frame-specific compactness value used in proximity scoring.

primitives.name: Bootstrap Uncertainty Quantifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: A 95% confidence interval was computed via bootstrap (resampling with replacement of each frame's contributions, 2,000 iterations) for the six leading players in the test match (table 4).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: CI: Confidence Interval (dimensionless probability), B: Bootstrap iterations (count = 2000), g_f: Frame contribution (minute-equivalents)
primitives.assumptions: Frame-level contributions are independent and identically distributed within the match context; sampling variability dominates short-term noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when inter-frame autocorrelation is extreme or when total match duration is insufficient to support asymptotic convergence of the empirical distribution.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI's conformal prediction sets, providing rigorous bounds on metric stability without relying on parametric Gaussian assumptions.
layer2.telemetry: Width of the 95% CI relative to the mean total.

primitives.name: Possession Phase Gravity Split
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the three forwards and attacking midfielders identifiable by their position in the overall ranking (Quiñones, Júnior, Retegui), gravity clearly concentrates during their own team's possession, up to double in Retegui's case
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: G_own: Gravity during own possession (minute-equivalents), G_opp: Gravity during opponent possession (minute-equivalents), R: Ratio G_own / G_opp (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Possession state is globally binary and accurately tracked; gravitational pull is strictly partitioned by the ball-holding team.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails during transitional chaos where possession tracking algorithms yield ambiguous states, or in set-pieces where static positioning decouples from dynamic possession flags.

layer2.mapping: Serves as a core feature vector for GSE's situational reasoning, distinguishing between offensive space-creators and defensive anchors based on phase-dependent density.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical Own/Opponent ratio per player role.

primitives.name: Defensive Anchor Inversion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Jedvaj carries more gravity during opponent possession (14.54 versus 8.41), consistent with a defender who draws opposing offensive pressure while defending, rather than a space-creator in attack.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: G_def_opp: Defensive gravity against opposition (minute-equivalents), G_def_own: Defensive gravity during own build-up (minute-equivalents)
primitives.assumptions: Defensive actions generate measurable spatial distortion even without ball contact; opponent offensive vectors are accurately captured.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Invalid for purely passive defenders who maintain shape without actively drawing pressure, resulting in uniformly low gravity across both phases.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's threat-mitigation kernels, identifying agents that successfully absorb and dissipate opposing kinetic energy.
layer2.telemetry: Negative deviation from the league-average Own/Opponent ratio.

primitives.name: Leave-One-Out Bias Corrector
primitives.verbatim_quote: Since the standard version is computationally simpler and player rank order does not change, this manuscript keeps the standard version as the primary definition, documents the leave-one-out version as a validated, available alternative, and recommends its use in any analysis where absolute magnitude, not only relative order, matters.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: G_std: Standard gravity total (minute-equivalents), G_loo: Leave-one-out corrected total (minute-equivalents)
primitives.assumptions: Self-interaction contributes a non-zero, systematic positive bias to the standard aggregate; removing it preserves ordinal rankings.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the metric relies heavily on self-proximity for baseline definition, causing LooO to drastically alter the underlying topology.

layer2.mapping: Provides GSI with a calibrated absolute scale for cross-match aggregation, neutralizing inflationary artifacts inherent in standard pairwise summation.
layer2.telemetry: Delta between G_std and G_loo as a percentage of total.

primitives.name: Offensive Gravity Proxy
primitives.verbatim_quote: It puts a number, for the first time, on something football has always known how to see but never known how to count.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{G}_i(t)': 'Offensive gravity of player i at time t, measured in arbitrary units', 'm_j': 'Mass of opponent j, dimensionless', 'd_{ij}(t)': 'Euclidean distance between player i and opponent j at time t, meters'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are modeled as point masses; opponents' influence decays quadratically with distance; baseline marking is dynamically updated per game state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( d_{ij}(t) \to 0 \), gravitational influence diverges; requires regularization for numerical stability.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's positional entropy kernel and GSI's influence probability density functions.
layer2.telemetry: Player positioning deviation from expected baseline under normal marking.

primitives.name: Dynamic Baseline Marking
primitives.verbatim_quote: The version of this manuscript an external reviewer first read had real errors: an unjustified fixed baseline, an undefined unit, zero sensitivity checks.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{B}(t)': 'Baseline marking configuration at time t, dimensionless', '\\vec{p}_i(t)': 'Position vector of player i at time t, meters', '\\vec{m}_i(t)': 'Marking position of opponent i at time t, meters'}
primitives.assumptions: Baseline is defined as minimal squared error between player and marking positions; compactness of marking varies across time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \mathcal{B}(t) \) becomes non-unique or unstable due to clustering.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to NBA's defensive positioning model under optical tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Compactness distribution variance across match intervals.

primitives.name: Positional Entropy Field
primitives.verbatim_quote: It demonstrates a way of working, not just a result.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{H}(t)': 'Entropy of player positions at time t, bits', 'p_i(t)': 'Probability of player i being in a given region at time t, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Positions are discretized into regions; entropy reflects spatial distribution uniformity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( p_i(t) \to 0 \) or \( p_i(t) \to 1 \), entropy approaches zero or infinity respectively.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's situational complexity score and GSI's entropy-based decision tree.
layer2.telemetry: Change in entropy over possession phases.

primitives.name: Construct Validity Check
primitives.verbatim_quote: They were flagged without evasion, and every single one of them was answered in this revision with verifiable empirical work on real data, not with more defensive prose.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{CVI}': 'Construct validity index, dimensionless', '\\rho(X, Y)': 'Pearson correlation between observed and predicted variables'}
primitives.assumptions: Validated through empirical data; constructs must align with theoretical expectations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \rho(X, Y) \to 0 \), construct validity is low.

reasoning_traces.think: The chapter window establishes the foundational epistemology of the gravitational metric, transitioning from raw computation to rigorous statistical validation. The derivation begins by acknowledging the inherent illusion of precision in continuous metrics derived from discrete, reasoned design choices. To counter this, a bootstrap resampling methodology is introduced, treating each temporal frame's contribution as an independent stochastic variable. This yields a 95% confidence interval that quantifies intra-match sampling variability, effectively bounding the 'noise' of the measurement process itself. However, the text astutely distinguishes this narrow computational uncertainty from the much broader, practically relevant uncertainty of inter-match variability—a limitation explicitly tied to data coverage constraints. Simultaneously, the window introduces a critical structural refinement: the leave-one-out correction. By excluding self-interactions, the metric corrects a systematic bias, ensuring that absolute magnitudes reflect true external influence rather than inflated self-proximity. This correction is proven robust as it preserves the ordinal ranking of players. Finally, the metric undergoes construct validity testing through a possession-phase split. The empirical observation that attackers concentrate gravity during own possession, while defenders invert this pattern during opponent possession, provides a powerful doctrinal anchor. It demonstrates that the abstract mathematical formalism successfully captures the intuitive, asymmetric nature of football roles, bridging the gap between geometric abstraction and tactical reality.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive lineage traces back to early spatiotemporal tracking attempts in the late 1990s, which struggled with noisy GPS data. It evolved through the adoption of computer vision-based optical tracking in the 2010s, enabling frame-by-frame positional accuracy. The specific gravitational analogy borrows from classical mechanics and agent-based modeling, adapting Newtonian concepts of mass and distance to quantify social and tactical 'pull' in team sports, moving beyond simple proximity metrics like Voronoi diagrams.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires recognizing that gravity is a zero-sum spatial contest. When a defender like Jedvaj exhibits high gravity during opponent possession, it implies a sophisticated understanding of off-ball movement designed to occupy the attacker's cognitive and physical space. Conversely, an attacker's high own-possession gravity reflects an intent to manipulate defensive shapes. The metric thus serves as a proxy for the player's ability to impose their will on the local geometry, anticipating and reacting to the opposing team's strategic intentions.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict anti-collinearity veto must be applied when correlating gravity splits with traditional volume metrics like pass count or touches. High gravity should not merely reflect playing time or ball proximity but distinct spatial distortion. Furthermore, leakage vetoes are required to ensure that the 'own possession' gravity of one team does not artifactually inflate due to the 'opponent possession' gravity of the other, given the mathematical identity that total pulls are symmetric across the pitch boundary.
